mcqs.question: What defines a combinational circuit, as opposed to a sequential one?
options: Its output depends only on its current inputs, with no internal memory of past inputs
It can only have one output signal
It must operate on a clock signal
mcqs.explanation: Combinational circuits are pure functions of their current inputs -- no state, no memory. Sequential circuits (the next topic) add feedback/memory so output also depends on history. Neither definition is about gate type, output count, or clocking specifically.

mcqs.question: What does a full adder have that a half adder doesn't?
options: A carry-in input, allowing it to be chained with other adders
The ability to add negative numbers
mcqs.explanation: Both half and full adders produce a sum and carry-out, and both use XOR internally. The key difference is the full adder accepts a carry-in, which is what makes chaining multiple adders together (ripple-carry) possible.

mcqs.question: Why is a multiplexer described as a 'universal function generator'?
options: Because it can only implement AND and OR functions
Because by wiring the right constants and signals into its data inputs, it can implement any boolean function of its select lines
Because it requires no select lines to operate
Because it can store data between clock cycles
mcqs.explanation: A mux with n select lines, given the right combination of constants and signal inputs, can realize any boolean function of those n variables -- which is why muxes appear at essentially every decision point in a datapath, beyond simple data routing.

mcqs.question: What is the main trade-off a carry-lookahead adder makes compared to a ripple-carry adder?
options: It uses fewer gates but is much slower
It uses more gates (for the lookahead logic) in exchange for much lower addition latency at wide bit widths
It can only add numbers up to 8 bits wide
It eliminates the need for a carry signal entirely
mcqs.explanation: Carry-lookahead adders compute carries directly from the inputs via extra generate/propagate logic, avoiding the ripple delay, but this costs additional gates -- a direct area-for-speed trade, which real wide ALUs make because addition latency caps clock speed.
